status: PRE-REGISTERED 2026-11-17, committed before the conversion model was fitted or any policy was evaluated on the split below. Edit only by writing v3.
relation_to_v1: hillstrom_protocol_v1.json stays valid for the visit method track (mi.experiments.hillstrom). v2 adds the buyer decision case HILLSTROM_EMAIL_2008 with conversion as the primary outcome. v1 code and report are not modified.
prior_exposure: REPEATED EVALUATION, not an untouched test. Before this protocol the team had already seen, under v1: full-sample average effects for visit, conversion and spend; a visit T-learner; and an exploratory conversion and spend T-learner at one 30% cap on a 50/50 split (seed 20080320), where the past-spend rule looked better than the model for the Mens e-mail and nothing was clearly separated from random. The published full-sample rates of the winning analysis were also known. The split below uses a new seed but overlaps the old held-out half.
business_question: Under a contact cap, which e-mail (Mens merchandise, Womens merchandise or none) should go to which existing customers, how many additional purchasing customers does that create versus no e-mail, and does the decision change with contact cost and margin?

source.terms: none stated on the source page (checked 2026-11-14 and 2026-11-17): raw file kept local and NOT committed or shared

unit: one row = one unique existing customer who last purchased within twelve months (source description). The file has no customer id: the zero-based row index is the customer key.
duplicates: Fully identical rows are counted and reported. They are KEPT: the source states one row per customer and there is no id to deduplicate on, so identical rows are treated as different customers with the same coarse attributes.
comparison_rule: Each e-mail is compared with the SAME no-e-mail control. Mens vs Womens is never reported as if one of them were untreated.

outcome.definition: 1 = the customer purchased merchandise in the two weeks following the e-mail campaign (source definition)
outcome.economics_only: spend (dollars in the same two weeks) is used only for incremental spend per contact; it is not a model target
outcome.not_used: visit (the v1 primary outcome) is not used in v2

features_pre_treatment.timing: all describe the twelve months BEFORE the e-mail (source definitions)
features_pre_treatment.meaning_note: mens / womens are past-year product purchase indicators, NOT the customer's gender

excluded.history_segment: pre-treatment but a binned copy of history; left out as redundant
excluded.segment: the randomized assignment; enters only as the treatment indicator, never as a customer feature
excluded.visit, conversion, spend: post-treatment outcomes; forbidden as predictors, as ranking inputs and in any preprocessing statistic

split.method: customer-level random split, stratified by arm
split.reason: the purchase rate is below 1.3%, so the test split is kept large; the model has about 30 coefficients and is refitted on train+validation (60%) before the test is read

model.type: one regularized (L2) logistic regression used as an S-learner for the three arms
model.design: intercept + 9 base features + 2 treatment indicators (Mens e-mail, Womens e-mail) + every treatment x base-feature interaction (18) = 29 coefficients
model.selection: fit each C on train; choose the C with the lowest validation log loss for conversion (ties: smaller C); refit once on train+validation with that C; no other tuning, no class weights
model.prediction: p(purchase | x, arm) for no e-mail, Mens e-mail and Womens e-mail; predicted uplift of an e-mail = p(x, that e-mail) - p(x, no e-mail)
model.interpretation: a conditional expected difference for customers like x, never an observed individual causal effect
model.no_other_models: no boosted trees, no second classifier, no LLM fine-tuning

choices_made_on_train_and_validation_onl.best_overall_arm: the e-mail with the larger conversion average effect versus control on train+validation
choices_made_on_train_and_validation_onl.primary_rule: of the recency rule and the history rule, the one with the larger uplift at the 25% cap on validation for the best overall arm

cap_rule: caps are fixed here and are not tuned to the test outcome; k = round(cap x number of held-out customers); selection is over all held-out customers of the three arms using pre-treatment information only

policies.NO_EMAIL: contact nobody (reference; zero additional buyers by definition)
policies.SEND_ALL: one e-mail to every eligible customer, reported for each e-mail
policies.RANDOM: one e-mail to a random share; its expected uplift per contact equals the held-out average effect, estimated on the whole held-out arms (more precise than one random draw)
policies.RULE_RECENCY: lowest recency (months since last purchase) first; ties by higher history, then row index
policies.RULE_HISTORY: highest history (past-year spend) first; ties by lower recency, then row index
policies.MODEL: highest predicted uplift for that e-mail first; ties by row index
policies.MODEL_BESTARM: each customer gets the e-mail with the higher predicted uplift; customers ranked by that uplift

estimators.single_arm_policy: inside the selected set S: mean(conversion | randomized to that e-mail) - mean(conversion | randomized to No E-Mail). This is uplift at k with the 'overall' strategy, selecting over all three arms.
estimators.multi_arm_policy: S is split by the e-mail the policy assigns (S_mens, S_womens). Estimate = sum over e-mails of |S_a|/|S| x mean(conversion | in S_a and randomized to a) - mean(conversion | in S and randomized to No E-Mail). Because assignment was randomized with equal probabilities, customers whose randomized arm equals the policy's arm are a random subsample of that arm's targets, so this is unbiased for the policy's value. Customers randomized to the other e-mail are not used.
estimators.primary_metric: additional purchasing customers per 1,000 customers contacted = 1000 x the estimate above
estimators.per_eligible: additional purchasing customers per 1,000 eligible customers = contact share x the per-contact figure
estimators.full_sample_average_effect: difference of arm purchase rates on all 64,000 customers, unpooled normal-approximation 95% interval

uncertainty.method: customer-level bootstrap of the test split: resample held-out customers with replacement, 2000 resamples, seed 20261117, percentile 95% interval
uncertainty.paired: differences between two policies are computed inside the same resamples
uncertainty.limit: policy scores are held fixed, so the interval covers test-sampling uncertainty only, not the variability of refitting the model

primary_comparison: at the 25% cap, for the best overall arm: MODEL versus RANDOM and MODEL versus the primary rule, in additional buyers per 1,000 contacts

decision_rule.MODEL_WIN_STABLE: the paired 95% intervals of (model - random) AND (model - primary rule) both lie above zero
decision_rule.MODEL_AHEAD_NOT_STABLE: both point differences are positive but at least one interval includes zero
decision_rule.NO_MODEL_ADVANTAGE: at least one point difference is zero or negative
decision_rule.consequence: Only MODEL_WIN_STABLE supports a model-targeted recommendation. Otherwise the recommendation falls back to the randomized average effect: the best overall arm for all eligible customers with a randomized no-e-mail holdout, provided its full-sample 95% interval excludes zero and cost per contact is verified to be below break-even. If the full-sample interval includes zero the recommendation is no e-mail / more evidence. No e-mail is always an allowed outcome.

secondary_analyses: Qini coefficient (area between the Qini curve and the random line, divided by the same area for the optimum curve without negative effects) for the model score and the primary rule score, each e-mail versus control, with a bootstrap interval
observed uplift by quartile of predicted uplift, per e-mail, on test
calibration: mean predicted versus observed purchase rate by arm on test

ONE descriptive segmentation on the full sample: average effect of each e-mail by past-year purchase category (Mens only, Womens only, both), with intervals and small-cell flags; hypothesis-generating only
small_cell_rule: any treated or control cell with fewer than 10 buyers is flagged small_cell_warning

economics.incremental_spend_per_contact: treated mean spend - control mean spend (experiment estimate)

assumption_sets.UNKNOWN_INPUTS: margin, cost and setup unknown -> contribution UNKNOWN (the current honest state)

economics.assumed_scale: mailable base 64,000 (the experiment population), 10% randomized holdout kept out of a broad send
economics.label: illustrative ASSUMPTIONS chosen by the project team; none comes from the dataset or a client; scenario contribution is never called measured profit

not_claimed: new-customer acquisition (every customer is an existing buyer)
any effect for the grocery retailer, FashionForward or a current 2026 customer base without a new randomized pilot
